sanskrit: tatas taṃ kalaśaṃ dṛṣṭvā jalapūrṇaṃ sa pārthivaḥ abhyadravata vegena pītvā cāmbho vyavāsṛjat
english: Then seeing that water-filled pot, the king rushed toward it swiftly, drank the water, and set it down.

sanskrit: sa pītvā śītalaṃ toyaṃ pipāsārto mahīpatiḥ nirvāṇam agamad dhīmān susukhī cābhavat tadā
english: Having drunk the cool water, that wise king — tormented by thirst — attained relief and became greatly content at that moment.

sanskrit: tatas te pratyabudhyanta ṛṣayaḥ sanarādhipāḥ nistoyaṃ taṃ ca kalaśaṃ dadṛśuḥ sarva eva te
english: Then those seers, together with the lord of the gods, awoke and all of them saw that the pot was empty of water.

sanskrit: kasya karmedam iti ca paryapṛcchan samāgatāḥ yuvanāśvo mayety eva satyaṃ samabhipadyata
english: Assembled together they asked, "Whose deed is this?" Yuvanāśva, speaking truth, admitted, "It was I."

sanskrit: na yuktam iti taṃ prāha bhagavān bhārgavas tadā sutārthaṃ sthāpitā hy āpas tapasā caiva saṃbhṛtāḥ
english: "This was not right," said the blessed Bhārgava to him then. "Those waters were stored for the purpose of a son, charged with the power of austerity."

sanskrit: mayā hy atrāhitaṃ brahma tapa āsthāya dāruṇam putrārthaṃ tava rājarṣe mahābalaparākrama
english: "By me here was sacred power infused through terrible austerity, for the sake of your son, O royal sage of great strength and valor."

sanskrit: mahābalo mahāvīryas tapobalasamanvitaḥ yaḥ śakram api vīryeṇa gamayed yamasādanam
english: "One who would be mighty in strength and valor, endowed with the power of asceticism, who could by his prowess send even Indra to the abode of Yama."

sanskrit: anena vidhinā rājan mayaitad upapāditam abbhakṣaṇaṃ tvayā rājann ayuktaṃ kṛtam adya vai
english: "By this rite, O king, was this prepared by me — the drinking of the water by you, O king, was indeed an improper act done today."

sanskrit: na tv adya śakyam asmābhir etat kartum ato 'nyathā nūnaṃ daivakṛtaṃ hy etad yad evaṃ kṛtavān asi
english: "But now it is not possible for us to undo this otherwise — surely this was wrought by fate, that you acted in this way."

sanskrit: pipāsitena yāḥ pītā vidhimantrapuraskṛtāḥ āpas tvayā mahārāja mattapovīryasaṃbhṛtāḥ tābhyas tvam ātmanā putram evaṃvīryaṃ janiṣyasi
english: "Those waters which you drank when thirsty, O great king, consecrated with sacred rites and mantras, charged with the power of my exalted austerity — from those waters you yourself shall beget a son of such prowess."

sanskrit: vidhāsyāmo vayaṃ tatra taveṣṭiṃ paramādbhutām yathā śakrasamaṃ putraṃ janayiṣyasi vīryavān
english: "We shall perform for you in that matter a most wondrous sacrificial rite, so that you, the valiant one, shall beget a son equal to Indra."

sanskrit: tato varṣaśate pūrṇe tasya rājño mahātmanaḥ vāmaṃ pārśvaṃ vinirbhidya sutaḥ sūrya ivāparaḥ
english: Then, when a full hundred years had elapsed, a son burst forth from the left side of that great-souled king, like a second sun.

sanskrit: niścakrāma mahātejā na ca taṃ mṛtyur āviśat yuvanāśvaṃ narapatiṃ tad adbhutam ivābhavat
english: The one of great radiance came forth, and death did not enter Yuvanāśva the lord of men — that seemed a marvel indeed.

sanskrit: tataḥ śakro mahātejās taṃ didṛkṣur upāgamat pradeśinīṃ tato 'syāsye śakraḥ samabhisaṃdadhe
english: Then Indra of great splendor came desiring to see him, and placed his index finger into the infant's mouth.

sanskrit: mām ayaṃ dhāsyatīty evaṃ paribhāṣṭaḥ sa vajriṇā māndhāteti ca nāmāsya cakruḥ sendrā divaukasaḥ
english: "This one shall suckle me" — thus declared the wielder of the thunderbolt, and the gods together with Indra gave the child the name Māndhātṛ.

sanskrit: pradeśinīṃ śakradattām āsvādya sa śiśus tadā avardhata mahīpāla kiṣkūṇāṃ ca trayodaśa
english: That infant, having tasted the finger given by Indra, grew, O lord of the earth, thirteen kiṣkus in a single day.

sanskrit: vedās taṃ sadhanurvedā divyāny astrāṇi ceśvaram upatasthur mahārāja dhyātamātrāṇi sarvaśaḥ
english: The Vedas along with the Dhanurveda, and the divine weapons, approached him as master, O great king, coming to him in all ways merely by his thought.

sanskrit: dhanur ājagavaṃ nāma śarāḥ śṛṅgodbhavāś ca ye abhedyaṃ kavacaṃ caiva sadyas tam upasaṃśrayan
english: The bow named Ājagava, the arrows sprung from horns, and an impenetrable armor — all these immediately came to attend upon him.

sanskrit: so 'bhiṣikto maghavatā svayaṃ śakreṇa bhārata dharmeṇa vyajayal lokāṃs trīn viṣṇur iva vikramaiḥ
english: He was consecrated by bountiful Indra himself, O Bhārata, and by righteousness he conquered the three worlds with strides like Viṣṇu.

sanskrit: tasyāpratihataṃ cakraṃ prāvartata mahātmanaḥ ratnāni caiva rājarṣiṃ svayam evopatasthire
english: The unstoppable wheel of that great soul set in motion, and jewels of their own accord came to attend upon the royal sage.

sanskrit: tasyeyaṃ vasusaṃpūrṇā vasudhā vasudhādhipa teneṣṭaṃ vividhair yajñair bahubhiḥ svāptadakṣiṇaiḥ
english: This earth full of wealth was his, O lord of the earth, and by him were performed many and varied sacrifices with abundant ritual fees.

sanskrit: citacaityo mahātejā dharmaṃ prāpya ca puṣkalam śakrasyārdhāsanaṃ rājaṃl labdhavān amitadyutiḥ
english: Having built altars and having attained abundant merit, that one of immeasurable radiance, O king, won a half-share of Indra's throne.

sanskrit: ekāhnā pṛthivī tena dharmanityena dhīmatā nirjitā śāsanād eva saratnākarapattanā
english: In a single day this steadfastly righteous wise one conquered, by mere command, the earth with all its jewel-bearing oceans and cities.

sanskrit: tasya cityair mahārāja kratūnāṃ dakṣiṇāvatām caturantā mahī vyāptā nāsīt kiṃ cid anāvṛtam
english: By his sacrificial fire-altars, O great king, of those rites with lavish gifts, the four-cornered earth was filled — there was nothing left uncovered.

sanskrit: tena padmasahasrāṇi gavāṃ daśa mahātmanā brāhmaṇebhyo mahārāja dattānīti pracakṣate
english: By that great-souled one, they say, O great king, ten thousand lotus-thousands of cows were given to the brahmins.

sanskrit: tena dvādaśavārṣikyām anāvṛṣṭyāṃ mahātmanā vṛṣṭaṃ sasyavivṛddhyarthaṃ miṣato vajrapāṇinaḥ
english: By that great-souled one, during a twelve-year drought, rain was caused to fall for the growth of crops, before the very eyes of the thunderbolt-bearer.

sanskrit: tena somakulotpanno gāndhārādhipatir mahān garjann iva mahāmeghaḥ pramathya nihataḥ śaraiḥ
english: By him the great lord of Gāndhāra, born of the Soma lineage, who roared like a great cloud, was overcome and slain with arrows.

sanskrit: prajāś caturvidhās tena jitā rājan mahātmanā tenātmatapasā lokāḥ sthāpitāś cāpi tejasā
english: The four kinds of subjects were conquered by him, O king, that great-souled one; by his self-austerity were the worlds also established in his splendor.

sanskrit: tasyaitad devayajanaṃ sthānam ādityavarcasaḥ paśya puṇyatame deśe kurukṣetrasya madhyataḥ
english: Here is that divine sacrificial ground, the site of that one radiant as the sun — behold it in the most sacred region, in the midst of Kurukṣetra.

sanskrit: etat te sarvam ākhyātaṃ māndhātuś caritaṃ mahat janma cāgryaṃ mahīpāla yan māṃ tvaṃ paripṛcchasi
english: All this has now been told to you — the great deeds of Māndhātṛ and his wondrous birth, O lord of the earth, which you asked me about.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca kathaṃvīryaḥ sa rājābhūt somako vadatāṃ vara karmāṇy asya prabhāvaṃ ca śrotum icchāmi tattvataḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Of what valor was that king Somaka, O best of speakers? I wish to hear in truth his deeds and his power.

sanskrit: lomaśa uvāca yudhiṣṭhirāsīn nṛpatiḥ somako nāma dhārmikaḥ tasya bhāryāśataṃ rājan sadṛśīnām abhūt tadā
english: Lomaśa said: O Yudhiṣṭhira, there was a righteous king named Somaka. He had a hundred wives of equal standing, O king.

sanskrit: sa vai yatnena mahatā tāsu putraṃ mahīpatiḥ kaṃ cin nāsādayām āsa kālena mahatā api
english: That lord of the earth, though striving with great effort among them, could not obtain even a single son even over a great span of time.

sanskrit: kadā cit tasya vṛddhasya yatamānasya yatnataḥ jantur nāma sutas tasmin strīśate samajāyata
english: Once, for that aged one striving with effort, a son named Jantu was born among that assembly of a hundred women.

sanskrit: taṃ jātaṃ mātaraḥ sarvāḥ parivārya samāsate satataṃ pṛṣṭhataḥ kṛtvā kāmabhogān viśāṃ pate
english: All the mothers constantly surrounded that newborn and sat attending him, setting aside their pleasures, O lord of the people.

sanskrit: tataḥ pipīlikā jantuṃ kadā cid adaśat sphiji sa daṣṭo vyanadad rājaṃs tena duḥkhena bālakaḥ
english: Then once an ant bit Jantu on the buttock, and the child, bitten, cried out, O king, in that pain.

sanskrit: tatas tā mātaraḥ sarvāḥ prākrośan bhṛśaduḥkhitāḥ parivārya jantuṃ sahitāḥ sa śabdas tumulo 'bhavat
english: Then all those mothers, deeply distressed, cried out together, surrounding Jantu, and there arose a tumultuous noise.

sanskrit: tam ārtanādaṃ sahasā śuśrāva sa mahīpatiḥ amātyapariṣanmadhye upaviṣṭaḥ sahartvijaiḥ
english: That distressed cry was suddenly heard by the lord of the earth, seated in the midst of his council of ministers along with his priests.

sanskrit: tataḥ prasthāpayām āsa kim etad iti pārthivaḥ tasmai kṣattā yathāvṛttam ācacakṣe sutaṃ prati
english: The king then sent someone asking "What is this?" and the chamberlain reported to him what had occurred regarding his son.

sanskrit: tvaramāṇaḥ sa cotthāya somakaḥ saha mantribhiḥ praviśyāntaḥpuraṃ putram āśvāsayad ariṃdamaḥ
english: Rising in haste, Somaka the subduer of enemies entered the inner apartments together with his ministers and consoled his son.

sanskrit: sāntvayitvā tu taṃ putraṃ niṣkramyāntaḥpurān nṛpaḥ ṛtvijaiḥ sahito rājan sahāmātya upāviśat
english: Having consoled the son, the king departed from the inner apartments, O king, and sat down together with his officiating priests and ministers.

sanskrit: somaka uvāca dhig astv ihaikaputratvam aputratvaṃ varaṃ bhavet nityāturatvād bhūtānāṃ śoka evaikaputratā
english: Somaka said: Shame on having only one son here! Sonlessness would be better. From the perpetual anxiety of all beings, having only one son is pure grief.

sanskrit: idaṃ bhāryāśataṃ brahman parīkṣyopacitaṃ prabho putrārthinā mayā voḍhaṃ na cāsāṃ vidyate prajā
english: "This hundred of wives, O brahmin, was taken by me after careful selection, O lord, desiring sons, yet there is no offspring from them."

sanskrit: ekaḥ kathaṃ cid utpannaḥ putro jantur ayaṃ mama yatamānasya sarvāsu kiṃ nu duḥkham ataḥ param
english: "Somehow one son, this Jantu, has been born to me despite my striving among all of them — what greater sorrow is there than this?"

sanskrit: vayaś ca samatītaṃ me sabhāryasya dvijottama āsāṃ prāṇāḥ samāyattā mama cātraikaputrake
english: "My age has passed together with my wives, O best of twice-born ones; the lives of all these women depend upon this one son of mine here."

sanskrit: syān nu karma tathā yuktaṃ yena putraśataṃ bhavet mahatā laghunā vāpi karmaṇā duṣkareṇa vā
english: "Is there any appropriate action, whether great or small, whether difficult or not, by which I might have a hundred sons?"

sanskrit: ṛtvig uvāca asti vai tādṛśaṃ karma yena putraśataṃ bhavet yadi śaknoṣi tat kartum atha vakṣyāmi somaka
english: The priest said: There is indeed such an action by which you could have a hundred sons. If you are able to do it, then I shall tell you, Somaka.

sanskrit: somaka uvāca kāryaṃ vā yadi vākāryaṃ yena putraśataṃ bhavet kṛtam eva hi tad viddhi bhagavān prabravītu me
english: Somaka said: Whether it is to be done or not to be done, if by it a hundred sons could be had — know that it is as good as done. Let the revered one tell me.

sanskrit: ṛtvig uvāca yajasva jantunā rājaṃs tvaṃ mayā vitate kratau tataḥ putraśataṃ śrīmad bhaviṣyaty acireṇa te
english: The priest said: Sacrifice with Jantu, O king, in a rite spread out by me. Then a glorious hundred sons will be yours before long.

sanskrit: vapāyāṃ hūyamānāyāṃ dhūmam āghrāya mātaraḥ tatas tāḥ sumahāvīryāñ janayiṣyanti te sutān
english: When the omentum is being offered and the mothers smell the smoke, they will then bear sons of very great valor for you.

sanskrit: tasyām eva tu te jantur bhavitā punar ātmajaḥ uttare cāsya sauvarṇaṃ lakṣma pārśve bhaviṣyati
english: "And Jantu himself will again be born as your son in that very womb, and a golden mark will appear on his right side."

sanskrit: somaka uvāca brahman yad yad yathā kāryaṃ tat tat kuru tathā tathā putrakāmatayā sarvaṃ kariṣyāmi vacas tava
english: Somaka said: O brahmin, whatever must be done and in whatever manner — do it just so. Desiring sons, I shall do all that you say.

sanskrit: lomaśa uvāca tataḥ sa yājayām āsa somakaṃ tena jantunā mātaras tu balāt putram apākarṣuḥ kṛpānvitāḥ
english: Lomaśa said: Then he caused Somaka to sacrifice with Jantu as the offering. But the mothers by force tried to pull away their son, overcome with compassion.

sanskrit: hā hatāḥ smeti vāśantyas tīvraśokasamanvitāḥ taṃ mātaraḥ pratyakarṣan gṛhītvā dakṣiṇe kare savye pāṇau gṛhītvā tu yājako 'pi sma karṣati
english: Crying out "Alas, we are slain!" filled with intense grief, the mothers pulled him back by the right hand, but the sacrificial priest too pulled by taking hold of the left hand.

sanskrit: kurarīṇām ivārtānām apākṛṣya tu taṃ sutam viśasya cainaṃ vidhinā vapām asya juhāva saḥ
english: Like distressed osprey-birds — having pulled away that son, he slew him according to the rite and offered his omentum into the fire.

sanskrit: vapāyāṃ hūyamānāyāṃ gandham āghrāya mātaraḥ ārtā nipetuḥ sahasā pṛthivyāṃ kurunandana sarvāś ca garbhān alabhaṃs tatas tāḥ pārthivāṅganāḥ
english: When the omentum was being offered, the mothers smelled the aroma and swooned suddenly to the ground in anguish, O delight of the Kurus; and all those royal women then conceived.

sanskrit: tato daśasu māseṣu somakasya viśāṃ pate jajñe putraśataṃ pūrṇaṃ tāsu sarvāsu bhārata
english: Then, within ten months, O lord of the people, a full hundred sons were born among all those wives of Somaka, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: jantur jyeṣṭhaḥ samabhavaj janitryām eva bhārata sa tāsām iṣṭa evāsīn na tathānye nijāḥ sutāḥ
english: Jantu was born again as the eldest, in his own mother, O Bhārata. He was dear to all of them in a way that no other natural sons were.

sanskrit: tac ca lakṣaṇam asyāsīt sauvarṇaṃ pārśva uttare tasmin putraśate cāgryaḥ sa babhūva guṇair yutaḥ
english: And that golden mark was there on his right side. Among that hundred sons he was preeminent, endowed with virtues.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa lokam agamat somakasya guruḥ param atha kāle vyatīte tu somako 'py agamat param
english: Then that teacher of Somaka departed to the highest world. And when time had passed, Somaka too departed to the beyond.

sanskrit: atha taṃ narake ghore pacyamānaṃ dadarśa saḥ tam apṛcchat kimarthaṃ tvaṃ narake pacyase dvija
english: And then he saw him being tormented in a terrible hell. He asked him: "For what reason are you being cooked in hell, O twice-born one?"

sanskrit: tam abravīd guruḥ so 'tha pacyamāno 'gninā bhṛśam tvaṃ mayā yājito rājaṃs tasyedaṃ karmaṇaḥ phalam
english: That teacher, being tortured greatly by fire, said to him: "You were caused to sacrifice by me, O king — this is the fruit of that action."

sanskrit: etac chrutvā sa rājarṣir dharmarājānam abravīt aham atra pravekṣyāmi mucyatāṃ mama yājakaḥ matkṛte hi mahābhāgaḥ pacyate narakāgninā
english: Hearing this, that royal sage said to the king of dharma: "I shall enter here — let my officiating priest be freed. For my sake this blessed one is being burned in the fire of hell."

sanskrit: dharma uvāca nānyaḥ kartuḥ phalaṃ rājann upabhuṅkte kadā cana imāni tava dṛśyante phalāni dadatāṃ vara
english: Dharma said: No one else ever experiences the fruit of the doer's act, O king. These rewards are seen as yours, O best of the generous.

sanskrit: somaka uvāca puṇyān na kāmaye lokān ṛte 'haṃ brahmavādinam icchāmy aham anenaiva saha vastuṃ surālaye
english: Somaka said: I do not desire the meritorious worlds without this speaker of sacred wisdom. I wish to dwell with him in the abode of the gods.

sanskrit: narake vā dharmarāja karmaṇāsya samo hy aham puṇyāpuṇyaphalaṃ deva samam astv āvayor idam
english: "Or in hell, O king of dharma, I am indeed equal to him in this deed. Let the fruit of merit and demerit be equal for us both, O god."

sanskrit: dharma uvāca yady evam īpsitaṃ rājan bhuṅkṣvāsya sahitaḥ phalam tulyakālaṃ sahānena paścāt prāpsyasi sadgatim
english: Dharma said: If such is your desire, O king, then enjoy his fruit together with him for equal time; thereafter you shall attain a good destination along with him.

sanskrit: lomaśa uvāca sa cakāra tathā sarvaṃ rājā rājīvalocanaḥ punaś ca lebhe lokān svān karmaṇā nirjitāñ śubhān saha tenaiva vipreṇa guruṇā sa gurupriyaḥ
english: Lomaśa said: That lotus-eyed king did all this accordingly, and once again won his own auspicious worlds earned by his deeds — together with that brahmin teacher, he who was dear to his guru.

sanskrit: eṣa tasyāśramaḥ puṇyo ya eṣo 'gre virājate kṣānta uṣyātra ṣaḍrātraṃ prāpnoti sugatiṃ naraḥ
english: This is that holy hermitage, this one that shines before us. A patient man who dwells here for six nights attains a good passage.

sanskrit: etasminn api rājendra vatsyāmo vigatajvarāḥ ṣaḍrātraṃ niyatātmānaḥ sajjībhava kurūdvaha
english: In this place too, O king of kings, we shall dwell free from fever for six nights with controlled minds. Make yourself ready, O foremost of the Kurus.

sanskrit: lomaśa uvāca asmin kila svayaṃ rājann iṣṭavān vai prajāpatiḥ satram iṣṭīkṛtaṃ nāma purā varṣasahasrikam
english: Lomaśa said: In this place, O king, Prajāpati himself formerly performed a satra called Iṣṭīkṛta, lasting a thousand years.

sanskrit: ambarīṣaś ca nābhāga iṣṭavān yamunām anu yajñaiś ca tapasā caiva parāṃ siddhim avāpa saḥ
english: And Ambarīṣa, son of Nābhāga, performed sacrifices along the Yamunā; through sacrifices and through austerity he attained the highest perfection.

sanskrit: deśo nāhuṣayajñānām ayaṃ puṇyatamo nṛpa yatreṣṭvā daśa padmāni sadasyebhyo nisṛṣṭavān
english: This region of the Nāhuṣa sacrifices is the most sacred, O king — here he sacrificed and gave away ten padmas to those assembled at the rite.

sanskrit: sārvabhaumasya kaunteya yayāter amitaujasaḥ spardhamānasya śakreṇa paśyedaṃ yajñavāstv iha
english: Behold here this sacrificial ground of Yayāti, the universal sovereign, O son of Kuntī, the one of immeasurable energy who rivaled Indra.

sanskrit: paśya nānāvidhākārair agnibhir nicitāṃ mahīm majjantīm iva cākrāntāṃ yayāter yajñakarmabhiḥ
english: Behold the earth covered over with fires of various forms, as if sinking, overwhelmed by the sacrificial acts of Yayāti.

sanskrit: eṣā śamy ekapatrā sā śarakaṃ caitad uttamam paśya rāmahradān etān paśya nārāyaṇāśramam
english: Here is the śamī tree with a single leaf; that is the finest śaraka reed. Behold these lakes of Rāma; behold the hermitage of Nārāyaṇa.

sanskrit: etad ārcīkaputrasya yogair vicarato mahīm apasarpaṇaṃ mahīpāla raupyāyām amitaujasaḥ
english: This, O lord of the earth, is the retreat of the son of Ṛcīka, the one of immeasurable energy, who wanders the earth through his yogic powers, at Raupyā.

sanskrit: atrānuvaṃśaṃ paṭhataḥ śṛṇu me kurunandana ulūkhalair ābharaṇaiḥ piśācī yad abhāṣata
english: Here, O delight of the Kurus, hear from me the lineage recitation — what the piśācī adorned with mortars spoke.

sanskrit: yugaṃdhare dadhi prāśya uṣitvā cācyutasthale tadvad bhūtilaye snātvā saputrā vastum icchasi
english: "Having eaten curds at Yugaṃdhara and having dwelt at the place of Acyuta, and likewise having bathed at Bhūtilaya, you wish to dwell there with your sons."

sanskrit: ekarātram uṣitveha dvitīyaṃ yadi vatsyasi etad vai te divā vṛttaṃ rātrau vṛttam ato 'nyathā
english: "Having dwelt here one night, if you will stay a second — what happened during the day shall happen differently for you at night."
